node.title: Re: making a regex work with Unicode
node.author: haukex
node.doctext:
As a first step, make sure Perl is reading the files as UTF-8, see the -C switch in [doc://perlrun]:

$ perl -CSD -pe's/(.{0,60})\b/$1\n/g' FILE

If that isn't enough, perhaps using the [doc://perlrebackslash#\X|\X] "Unicode extended grapheme cluster" and/or [doc://perlrebackslash#\b{wb}|\b{wb}] "Unicode Word Boundary" will further help - I've never used them so far, but a quick test on a simple file worked for me:

$ perl -CSD -pe's/(\X{0,60})\b{wb}/$1\n/g' FILE

(As I was writing this, [poj] [id://1182843|wrote] about [doc://Text::Wrap], which also appears to have Unicode support, so that might be easiest.)
